To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density of CD8(+) tumor-infiltrating T lymphocytes is significantly correlated with the size of the tumor, the degree of lymph node metastasis, and the clinical stage of oral squamous cell carcinomas.
PD-L1 expression by OSCC cells was associated with the density of CD8(+) intratumoral T lymphocytes and that the PD-L1 expression was related to tumor size.

the densities of CD8(+)TILs in OSCC are associated with lymph node metastases, tumor size, and clinical stages and that PD-L1 expressed in OSCC cells is associated with a decreased number of intraturnoral TILs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the density of TILs and PD-L1 expression in OSCC.
the relationship between PD-L1 expression in OSCC and the density of tumor-infiltrating T lymphocytes.
the relationship between the expression of PD-L1, TILs and TAFs, which are involved in the immune reactions of OSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of PD-L1 by tumor cells is associated with the degree of tumor-infiltrating TILs and that this association may be an important factor in the prognosis of OSCC.
PD-L1 expression by OSCC cells is a significant prognostic factor for the survival of patients with OSCC.
PD-L1 expressed on OSCC cells may be associated with the development of lymph node metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TILs are important for the prognosis of OSCC patients and PD-L1 expressed on TAFs might play a role in inhibiting the antitumor immune response of OSCC patients.
PD-L1 expression by OSCC cells may inhibit the function of TILs.
PD-L1 expression by tumor cells and TILs is correlated with tumor progression and the prognosis of patients with OSCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PD-L1 expression in tumor-associated fibroblastic cells may be a potential target for the treatment of OSCC.
PD-L1 expression is associated with decreased numbers of intratumoral lymphocytes.
the expression of PD-L1 on tumor cells is associated with the number of CD8(+) intratumoral T lymphocytes, and this association is independent of TAFs, which also express PD-L1.
